name: Setmelanotide

b.x: Mean body weight dropped 25.6% in POMC-deficient patients at 52 weeks (Clement et al. 2020, n=21) [1]. LEPR-deficient patients saw 12.5%. These are patients who experienced pathological, constant hunger from birth with no effective treatment until setmelanotide arrived. Setmelanotide (brand name IMCIVREE, CAS 920014-72-8) is a cyclic 8-amino-acid peptide analog of alpha-melanocyte stimulating hormone (alpha-MSH). It is a selective agonist at MC4R in the hypothalamus, the receptor that normally receives alpha-MSH to trigger satiety. In patients with POMC, PCSK1, or LEPR deficiency, the upstream pathway producing that alpha-MSH signal is broken. Setmelanotide steps in as a synthetic replacement, directly activating the receptor these patients can't reach on their own. The approved patient population keeps expanding. November 2020 brought initial approval for POMC, PCSK1, and LEPR deficiency obesity in patients aged 6 and older. Bardet-Biedl syndrome followed in 2022 (Haqq et al., n=44) [2]. The VENTURE trial (n=12) [3] extended approval down to age 2 in December 2024. Most recently, the TRANSCEND Phase 3 (n=120) secured acquired hypothalamic obesity approval in March 2026, showing an 18.4% placebo-adjusted BMI reduction. Specificity is the defining characteristic. Phase 2 trials in non-syndromic obesity showed minimal results. The EMANATE trial in March 2026 failed all four primary endpoints in heterozygous variant carriers. Setmelanotide works when the MC4R pathway is genuinely broken, not when it's functioning normally.

In normal physiology, leptin activates POMC neurons in the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus. Those neurons produce alpha-MSH, which travels to the paraventricular nucleus and binds MC4R. That binding event triggers satiety and increases energy expenditure. The entire cascade depends on each link working; a genetic defect at POMC, PCSK1, or LEPR breaks the chain before alpha-MSH ever reaches MC4R. Setmelanotide bypasses every upstream defect. It binds MC4R directly, restoring the satiety signal regardless of whether the patient can produce functional leptin responses, POMC protein, or processed alpha-MSH. The cyclic disulfide-bridged structure gives it proteolytic stability that native alpha-MSH lacks. Selectivity is relative. Setmelanotide activates MC4R preferentially, but it also hits MC1R on melanocytes and MC3R to a lesser degree. MC1R activation drives melanin production, which is why roughly 61 to 83% of treated patients develop skin hyperpigmentation. That side effect is mechanistic and expected; it reverses after stopping treatment. Plasma half-life sits at approximately 11 hours (FDA label, Section 12.3). Protein binding is 79.1%, with a volume of distribution around 49 to 75 L. Steady-state concentration is reached within about 2 days of daily dosing. The drug is cleared through proteolytic catabolism rather than CYP enzyme metabolism, which keeps the drug interaction profile low.
Setmelanotide benefits center on restoring satiety in patients with specific genetic defects in the melanocortin pathway.
Only FDA-approved therapy targeting MC4R for POMC, PCSK1, LEPR deficiency, Bardet-Biedl syndrome, and acquired hypothalamic obesity. No alternative treatments exist for these populations.
Mean 25.6% body weight reduction at 52 weeks in POMC-deficient patients, with 80% achieving at least 10% weight loss (Clement et al. 2020, n=21) [1].

Hunger score reduction of 27 to 44% in clinical trials. Caregivers describe children feeling satiated for the first time in their lives; quality of life improvements were detectable by week 5 in trial data.
Approved down to age 2 following the VENTURE trial (n=12) [3], where 83% of children achieved a clinically meaningful BMI Z-score reduction at 52 weeks.

The TRANSCEND Phase 3 (n=120) delivered an 18.4% placebo-adjusted BMI reduction in acquired hypothalamic obesity, opening treatment to patients with craniopharyngioma-related or trauma-related hypothalamic injury.

No tolerance or tachyphylaxis observed in any trial through the longest follow-up periods. Open-label extension and real-world cohort data (n=17, mean 14.4 months) [4] confirm durable appetite suppression.
Aligned
Scientific Evidence
Based on 6 key studies · FDA-approved
FDA-approved for POMC/PCSK1/LEPR deficiency obesity, Bardet-Biedl syndrome, and (March 2026) acquired hypothalamic obesity.

Dosing studied: Adults and adolescents ≥12: start 2 mg SC daily × 2 weeks → 3 mg/day (max). Children 6–<12: start 1 mg × 2 weeks → 2 mg → 3 mg/day once 2 mg is tolerated. Children 2–<6: start 0.5 mg → 0.5 to 2 mg/day by baseline body weight (label Table 3). Acquired hypothalamic obesity ages ≥4: start 0.5 mg daily × 2 weeks, then titrate per the label tables to 3 mg (ages 6 and up).

Phase 3 data in confirmed-genetic patients: mean −25.6% weight at 52 weeks (POMC deficiency), −12.5% (LEPR deficiency), −18.4% placebo-adjusted BMI (hypothalamic obesity). Efficacy is strictly limited to approved genetically confirmed or injury-defined populations: fails in common polygenic obesity and failed EMANATE heterozygous substudies (March 2026).
Key Study

Clement et al. 2020 (PMID 33137293): Phase 3, POMC/LEPR deficiency, n=21; 80% of POMC patients achieved ≥10% weight loss at 52 wks, mean −25.6%. Haqq et al. 2022 (PMID 36356613): Phase 3 BBS, n=44; 44.4% achieved ≥10% weight loss vs 0% placebo. VENTURE (PMID 39549719, Lancet DE 2025): n=12 ages 2–5; 83% achieved ≥0.2 BMI-Z reduction at 52 wks. TRANSCEND (2026): hypothalamic obesity n=120; −18.4% placebo-adjusted BMI.
Limitations

Efficacy limited to patients with confirmed pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in POMC, PCSK1, LEPR, BBS-associated genes, or confirmed hypothalamic injury. No efficacy in common polygenic obesity. EMANATE trial (March 2026) failed all 4 primary endpoints in heterozygous variant carriers (POMC/PCSK1 hets, LEPR hets, SRC1/NCOA1, SH2B1). Trial populations very small due to ultra-rare disease prevalence. Long-term safety beyond 3–4 years limited.
Community Experience
Extremely small online community (ultra-rare patient population: <30 Reddit threads).
Community dosing: 1–3 mg daily SC; clinical community follows FDA label exactly (no off-label dosing patterns documented)

Structured stakeholder data from 41 caregivers (CADTH 2023) shows near-universal positive sentiment; 95% would recommend. Primary complaints are hyperpigmentation, daily injection burden, and insurance/access barriers, not drug effectiveness. No off-label community use documented.
What users report (5)
Patients report feeling satiated for the first time in their lives: described as life-changing by caregivers
Substantial sustained weight loss with no tolerance observed at 1+ year follow-up
Quality of life improvements within 5 weeks: improved focus, mobility, social participation
Reduction in family stress from managing constant food-seeking/hyperphagia behaviors
Only effective treatment option for this population (no comparator alternatives exist)
Common issues (5)
Hyperpigmentation (skin darkening) in ~61–83%: cosmetically distressing, especially in lighter-skinned patients
Daily injection burden: particularly challenging for vision-impaired BBS patients and young children
Insurance prior authorization hurdles and extreme cost (~$419K–$429K/year without assistance)
GI upset (nausea, diarrhea) common during first 2–4 weeks at each dose level
Lifelong dependency: stopping causes rapid return of hyperphagia and weight regain within days to weeks
Science & Community Aligned

Scientific data and community reports are tightly aligned. Both confirm dramatic hunger suppression and significant weight loss in confirmed-genetic patients. Community-reported side effects (hyperpigmentation, GI effects, injection reactions) match clinical trial AE profiles exactly. No community reports of off-label use for common obesity, consistent with clinical findings that it does not work for that indication.

b.x: No reconstitution needed. IMCIVREE ships as a ready-to-inject 10 mg/mL solution in multi-dose vials. That's one less variable to manage. If you receive a lyophilized powder claiming to be setmelanotide, it is not the FDA-approved product. Syringe math for the 10 mg/mL vial using a U-100 insulin syringe: 1 mg equals 10 units (0.1 mL), 2 mg equals 20 units (0.2 mL), 3 mg equals 30 units (0.3 mL). Each vial contains 10 mg total. Inject in the morning. The 11-hour half-life means drug levels peak around 8 hours post-dose. Morning dosing aligns appetite suppression with daytime eating patterns. Store unopened vials at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius. Once out of the refrigerator, a vial can stay at 2 to 25 degrees Celsius for up to 30 days, with brief excursions up to 30 degrees Celsius. Discard it 30 days after first opening, regardless of remaining volume. This drug requires confirmed genetic testing before prescribing. Rhythm Pharmaceuticals provides free genetic testing through their IMCIVREE support program. You can't skip that step; setmelanotide won't help without a confirmed pathogenic variant.
Cycling Protocol
Designed for continuous daily use in patients with confirmed genetic obesity. Discontinuation leads to return of hyperphagia and weight regain. Treatment is lifelong in responders.
Setmelanotide Cycle

Setmelanotide is not cycled. It is a chronic replacement therapy providing the MC4R signal that patients are constitutionally missing (genetic indications) or have lost (hypothalamic injury). Continuous daily dosing is required to maintain appetite suppression. Stopping causes rapid return of pathological hyperphagia and weight regain: typically within days to weeks. There is no receptor desensitization, antibody formation, hormonal axis suppression, or safety-monitoring concern that would necessitate cycling. Cycling would be therapeutically counterproductive.
Rapid return of constant hunger/hyperphagia within days of missed doses or stopping
Weight regain begins quickly after discontinuation
Treatment is designed and labeled as lifelong in confirmed responders

Draw the correct dose into a U-100 insulin syringe Adults and adolescents 12 and older: start at 20 units (2 mg, 0.2 mL) daily for 2 weeks. Children 6 to under 12: start at 10 units (1 mg, 0.1 mL). Children 2 to under 6: start at 5 units (0.5 mg, 0.05 mL).

Use a 1 mL syringe with a 28 or 29 gauge needle for subcutaneous injection (label section 2.5). Pinch skin at the abdomen, thigh, or upper arm. Insert the needle straight in at a 90-degree angle (IMCIVREE Instructions for Use). Inject slowly. Rotate injection sites with each dose.
Inject once daily in the morning Appetite suppression onset tracks with Tmax (approximately 8 hours), so morning dosing covers daytime eating hours.

After 2 weeks, if the starting dose is tolerated, increase per protocol. Adults and adolescents: increase to 30 units (3 mg, 0.3 mL). Children 6 to under 12: increase to 20 units (2 mg). If 2 mg is tolerated, increase to 30 units (3 mg), the maintenance dose; if not, reduce to 10 units (1 mg) (label section 2.3). Children 2 to under 6: the dose then follows baseline body weight (label Table 3), rising 5 units (0.5 mg) every 2 weeks. It stops at 5 units (0.5 mg) for 15 to under 20 kg and 10 units (1 mg) for 20 to under 30 kg. It stops at 15 units (1.5 mg) for 30 to under 40 kg and 20 units (2 mg) for 40 kg and up.
Assess response at 16 weeks Discontinue if body weight reduction is less than 5% (adults) or BMI Z-score reduction is inadequate (children) at maximum tolerated dose.

GLP-1 agonists added to setmelanotide (off-label combination)

No clinical evidence for combination benefit. GLP-1s were inadequate monotherapy in POMC/LEPR-deficient patients prior to starting setmelanotide in clinical trials, as the MC4R pathway defect is not addressed by incretin mechanisms. No safety data on combination. Monitoring for additive GI side effects would be required if co-prescribed.

Depression and suicidal ideation carry an FDA-labeled warning. Patients must be screened for major depressive disorder at each clinic visit. Pediatric patients and those with acquired hypothalamic obesity (where pre-existing hypothalamic injury may complicate mental health assessment) require particularly close monitoring. This warning is non-negotiable. Priapism in male patients is a medical emergency. Spontaneous penile erections occur due to MC4R's role in sexual function. An erection lasting 4 hours or more requires urgent urological evaluation; untreated priapism causes permanent vascular damage. If recurring spontaneous erections (under 4 hours) develop, discuss dose reduction with the prescriber. Skin hyperpigmentation is the most common effect, reported in approximately 61% of trial patients and up to 83% in some datasets. MC1R activation in melanocytes drives melanin production. The darkening is cosmetic, not associated with malignancy, and reverses after stopping treatment. Baseline skin and ophthalmic exams are required before starting. Annual dermatology follow-up monitors pre-existing nevi for changes, as rare reports of darkening of existing moles appear in the prescribing information. Injection site reactions (erythema, pruritus) affect roughly 48% of patients. Rotating injection sites between abdomen, thigh, and upper arm reduces occurrence over time. Gastrointestinal symptoms include nausea, diarrhea, and abdominal pain. These are most pronounced during the first 2 to 4 weeks at each dose level. Following the FDA-labeled 2-week titration steps reduces severity. If symptoms are intolerable at 3 mg, remaining at 2 mg is acceptable per label. Published side effect data comes from Phase 3 trials in ultra-rare patient populations (combined enrollment across trials: approximately 200 patients). Long-term safety data beyond 3 to 4 years remains limited. Caregiver survey data (n=41, CADTH NBK599842) confirms the clinical trial AE profile without adding new safety signals. Contraindications: known hypersensitivity to setmelanotide or excipients, obesity not caused by approved genetic or hypothalamic indications (will not work), pregnancy (discontinue if pregnancy occurs), and active major depressive disorder or suicidal ideation (monitor closely if initiating). Kidney function changes the dose. Exposure rises 13 to 96% with renal impairment, and the label lowers the dose when it is severe (eGFR 15 to 29). For BBS or POMC, PCSK1 or LEPR deficiency, the start is 0.5 mg daily. Maintenance is 1.5 mg daily from age 12 and 1 mg daily for ages 6 to under 12. Children 2 to under 6 stay at 0.5 mg if they weigh 20 to under 30 kg; at 30 kg or more they move to 1 mg from week 3. With severe impairment, the label does not recommend it for acquired hypothalamic obesity or for children 2 to under 6 who weigh under 20 kg. IMCIVREE is not recommended at all in end-stage renal disease (eGFR under 15). Mild or moderate impairment needs no change (IMCIVREE label 2.4 and Table 4, 8.6). When to seek medical attention: erection lasting 4 hours or more (emergency), new or worsening depression or suicidal thoughts, new or changing skin moles, and persistent severe GI symptoms not resolving with dose titration.
Common Issues & Solutions

Hyperpigmentation appears in ~61–83% of patients. It is reversible upon discontinuation, cosmetic only, and not associated with malignancy. Baseline skin and eye exam required before starting; annual dermatology follow-up recommended for monitoring pre-existing nevi. Cannot be prevented: it is mechanistic (MC1R activation).

Priapism (erection lasting ≥4 hours) in male patients is a medical emergency: go to the ER immediately. Do not confuse with milder "spontaneous erections" listed in the FDA label; priapism causes permanent vascular damage if untreated. If spontaneous erections are recurring (but <4 hours), discuss dose reduction with prescriber.

GI symptoms (nausea, diarrhea, abdominal pain) are most common during the first 2–4 weeks at each dose level. Following the FDA 2-week titration steps minimizes severity. If intolerable at 3 mg, remain at 2 mg: there is no requirement to reach maximum dose for efficacy.

Inadequate weight loss (<5% at 16 weeks at maximum tolerated dose): first confirm the genetic diagnosis is appropriate (pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant confirmed by CLIA-certified laboratory). Confirm injection technique and dose accuracy with a specialty pharmacist. Per label, discontinue if confirmed non-responder.

Insurance denial or access barrier: Rhythm InTune patient access program offers free genetic testing, specialty pharmacy navigation, and copay support. Patient assistance programs can reduce cost substantially for eligible patients.

Setmelanotide is FDA-approved under the brand name IMCIVREE (Rhythm Pharmaceuticals). Initial approval came in November 2020 for POMC, PCSK1, and LEPR deficiency obesity in patients aged 6 and older. Bardet-Biedl syndrome was added in June 2022. The age range expanded to 2 and older in December 2024 following the VENTURE trial. Acquired hypothalamic obesity in patients aged 4 and older was approved in March 2026 per the TRANSCEND Phase 3 results. IMCIVREE is distributed through specialty pharmacies only. It is not available through standard retail pharmacies or compounding pharmacies. No compounded versions exist; setmelanotide is not on the FDA shortage list or the 503B bulk substances list. Research-grade setmelanotide acetate (CAS 920014-72-8) is sold only as a lab reagent for research and is not appropriate for human use. Annual cost runs approximately $419,000 to $429,000 at retail. Rhythm InTune patient access program and other patient assistance programs offer financial assistance to eligible patients. WADA status: not currently listed on the prohibited substance list, though athletes should verify with their governing body. protocols.monitoringNotes: Monthly weight and BMI. Baseline pituitary/hypothalamic endocrine panel (given underlying hypothalamic disorder). Careful depression monitoring: pre-existing hypothalamic injury may complicate mental health assessment. Male patients: assess for spontaneous erections.

faqs.q: How do we confirm our child has a qualifying genetic mutation?
faqs.a: Rhythm Pharmaceuticals provides free genetic testing through its IMCIVREE support program. Testing typically involves whole exome sequencing or targeted gene panels for POMC, PCSK1, LEPR, and BBS-associated genes. A confirmed pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant is required before prescribing: setmelanotide doesn't work for common polygenic obesity.

faqs.q: Will the skin darkening go away?
faqs.a: Yes: hyperpigmentation reverses after stopping. It comes from MC1R activation in melanocytes (not the therapeutic MC4R target) and is cosmetic, not associated with malignancy. The label recommends baseline skin and eye exams because of rare reports of darkening of pre-existing nevi.

faqs.q: Does my child have to take this medication forever?
faqs.a: In responders, yes: it's designed to be lifelong. When you stop setmelanotide, the pathological constant hunger (hyperphagia) returns quickly and weight is regained. The drug replaces a missing molecular signal; it doesn't fix the underlying genetic defect.

faqs.q: What should we do about spontaneous prolonged erections in male patients?
faqs.a: Spontaneous penile erections are listed on the FDA label. If an erection lasts more than 4 hours, that's priapism: a medical emergency requiring urgent urological evaluation. Patients and caregivers should be counseled about this at initiation. Dose reduction may be needed if it recurs.

faqs.q: Can setmelanotide be used off-label for regular obesity?
faqs.a: No, and this can't be stressed enough. The MC4R pathway activation only works when upstream signaling (POMC to alpha-MSH to MC4R) is disrupted by a genetic defect. In people with intact signaling, the pathway is already functional: adding a synthetic agonist doesn't produce the same dramatic effects. Phase 2 trials in non-syndromic obesity showed minimal efficacy.

faqs.q: What is the recommended Setmelanotide dosage?
faqs.a: Setmelanotide dosing varies by experience level. Beginners typically start at 2 mg daily, moderate users at 2 mg daily, and aggressive protocols use 3 mg daily.

faqs.q: Does Setmelanotide need to be reconstituted?
faqs.a: No. IMCIVREE comes as a ready-to-inject 10 mg/mL solution, 10mg in a 1 mL multiple-dose vial. Each dose is drawn straight from the vial: 1 mg is 0.1 mL, 10 units on a U-100 syringe.

faqs.q: What is the half-life of Setmelanotide?
faqs.a: The half-life of Setmelanotide is ~11 hours. This determines how frequently you need to dose for consistent blood levels.

summary: Eighty percent of POMC-deficient patients lost at least 10% of their body weight at one year. For a population with zero prior treatment options and lifelong unrelenting hunger, that number landed differently. Setmelanotide (IMCIVREE) is an 8-amino-acid cyclic peptide that directly activates the melanocortin-4 receptor in the hypothalamus, restoring the satiety signal these patients were born without. It earned FDA approval in November 2020 for POMC, PCSK1, and LEPR deficiency obesity, expanded to Bardet-Biedl syndrome in 2022, and picked up acquired hypothalamic obesity in March 2026. This drug does not work for common obesity. It replaces a missing molecular signal, not a behavioral one.
